targetAudience.primary: Architects and engineers building long-running agent runtimes, asynchronous progress delivery and replayable conversation systems
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands model turns, tool calls, event streams and conversation history.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A user-visible progress message may need durable audit history without being echoed into later model requests as if the model had reasoned over it.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change adds a gated asynchronous user-message tool whose typed delivery record survives protocol and history paths while its visible text is excluded from the next model request.

externalHook.description: What the user was told and what the model reasons over are related facts, but treating them as the same history stream creates false context and weak audit semantics.

coreProposition: Long-running agent systems should separate the user-delivery plane from the model reasoning-context plane while correlating both through stable message identity and replayable metadata; local acceptance or emission is not evidence of external delivery.

originalValue.description: Separates local message acceptance, user-facing delivery, model reasoning context and durable replay evidence into correlated but non-equivalent planes.

readerTakeaway: Persist a typed message identity and delivery classification, keep user delivery out of model context by default, and collect separate receipts for external delivery, acknowledgement and retry outcomes.

supported: The merged Codex tool is root-only and gated by feature and model support.
A valid call creates a typed asynchronous AgentMessage item and locally emits its lifecycle before returning accepted=true.
Integration tests show the visible text is not synthesized into the next model request.
Protocol, app-server and thread-history paths preserve delivery classification.
unsupported: Global ordering across clients and threads
uncertain: Which component owns final user-facing delivery receipts
How delivered facts should enter later reasoning when genuinely needed

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article concerns a general agent-runtime separation and needs no first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged mechanism is concrete and timely, and the Research Object adds a reusable model for separating communication, reasoning context and delivery evidence.
